title: Panes open in the wrong directory on Windows: path form
description:
Every pane on Windows starts in the MSYS home instead of the repo, silently. Agents would read and edit the wrong tree, or an empty one.

Cause: roles.mjs resolves repo with node's path.resolve(), which under a Windows node returns a Windows-form path (C:\Users\...\afox). fleet.sh passes that to tmux -c. MSYS2's tmux cannot chdir to a Windows-form path and falls back to $HOME without an error.

The fix is not a global conversion, because the two paths need OPPOSITE treatment: repo is consumed by MSYS tmux and must be POSIX form (/c/Users/...), while CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is consumed by claude.exe, a native Windows binary, and must stay Windows form. cygpath -u at the tmux boundary only.
acceptance_criteria: tmux list-panes -F '#{pane_current_path}' on a Windows fleet shows the repo for every pane. Both forms tested, not just the one that works.
notes: Observed 2026-09-18 on the five-pane local fleet: every pane reported cwd=/home/yoga. Isolated directly afterwards - 'tmux new-window -c C:\Users\unmii\spike\afox-lf' produced a pane at /home/yoga, and 'tmux new-window -c /c/Users/unmii/spike/afox-lf' produced one at /c/Users/unmii/spike/afox-lf. Same tmux, same session, one call apart. This is README gotcha 3 with a Windows cause.

title: Line endings break afox on Windows: CRLF checkout
description:
git on Windows checks out CRLF by default, and the repo has no .gitattributes. Two separate failures, both silent:

1. roles.mjs cannot parse roles.yml. Its top-level scalar regex is /^([A-Za-z_][\w-]*):\s*(.*)$/ - the (.*) cannot match a carriage return and $ does not match before one, so every top-level key fails to match and falls through to the ignore branch. Result: 'roles.yml: missing "repo"' followed by 'roles.mjs produced no roles', on a file where repo: . is plainly present.

2. Every script's shebang becomes '#!/usr/bin/env zsh\r', so ./fleet.sh fails with a bad interpreter error naming a shell that is installed. Only an explicit 'zsh ./fleet.sh' works.

Fix is a .gitattributes pinning LF for the files that are read by a shell or by a line-oriented parser - *.sh, *.mjs, *.yml, tmux.conf at minimum. Note this rewrites line endings in the working tree on the next checkout, so land it when the tree is clean.
acceptance_criteria: With a fresh clone on Windows, ./fleet.sh runs without a bad-interpreter error and FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 composes all five pane commands. Proven on a clone, not on a hand-converted copy.
notes: Both failures observed on this machine 2026-09-18. Proof of (1): node -e on the exact regex returns '.' for 'repo: .' and NO MATCH for 'repo: .\r'. Proof of (2): od -c on fleet.sh shows 'z s h \r \n' at the end of the shebang line. An LF copy of the nine scripts in a temp directory ran clean both ways - see afox-r0s.

title: Windows 11 prerequisites for afox
description:
Inventory of what afox needs on Windows 11 with no WSL, and what is missing. Measured on this machine 2026-09-18.

Present: node 26.7.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.55.0, Git Bash (MSYS2 bash 5.3), perl, timeout, awk, sed, Windows PowerShell 5.1. Provider CLIs present: claude, codex, ollama.
Absent: tmux, zsh, uuidgen, WSL, pwsh 7, go, docker. Provider CLIs absent: devin, gemini, goose, opencode.

Open items beyond the raw list:
- ~/.tmux.conf is created by fleet.sh as a symlink; on Windows that needs Developer Mode or an elevated shell, otherwise ln silently produces a copy or fails.
- The cost manifest path is ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/afox-fleet-*.json. TMPDIR is normally unset on Windows, so it falls back to /tmp, which under MSYS2 is a private mount, not C:\Temp - fine, but it means a Windows-native node process and an MSYS node process disagree about where the manifest is.
- cost.mjs resolves provider session logs from node's homedir(); MSYS node and Windows node return different roots, so the log discovery has to be pinned to one of them.
acceptance_criteria: A written prerequisite list in the repo that someone can follow on a clean Windows 11 box to the point where FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh composes every pane command without error. Each missing item either installed, replaced, or recorded as not needed.
notes:
Measured during the afox-r0s spike, 2026-09-18. Three prerequisites that are not obvious from the tool list:

1. MSYS2 installs without admin. The msys2-x86_64-latest.tar.xz base archive extracts anywhere the user can write (used C:\Users\unmii\msys64); only the .exe installer wants C:\ root and therefore admin. Bootstrap by running its bash once - but from a NATIVE Windows process, not from Git Bash: Git Bash is itself MSYS and the two msys-2.0.dll copies collide, which presents as a hang with no output and no error.

2. MSYS2 does not inherit the Windows PATH. node, claude and codex are all invisible in a default MSYS2 login shell, so fleet.sh dies at its own 'node required to read roles.yml' guard. Either set MSYS2_PATH_TYPE=inherit or add the specific directories: /c/Program Files/nodejs, /c/Users/<user>/.local/bin, /c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Links, /c/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm.

3. Developer Mode is NOT sufficient for symlinks. With Developer Mode already on, MSYS2's ln -s still produced a 204-byte regular copy; the same command under MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict produced a real 38-byte symlink. fleet.sh re-points ~/.tmux.conf on every run precisely so a stale config cannot go unnoticed, and a copy defeats that silently - the repo's tmux.conf edits simply stop arriving. Observed: /home/yoga/.tmux.conf was a plain 210-byte copy after the first dry run, and the second run warned that it is not a symlink.

Also note MSYS $HOME is /home/<user> inside msys64, NOT C:\Users\<user>. Windows binaries launched from MSYS2 still resolve their own home from USERPROFILE, so claude found its credentials correctly - but any shell-side ~ in afox's config means the msys64 home.

title: Beads on Windows: install, configure, state tracked in the repo
description:
bd was installed only on the Mac. On this Windows 11 machine there was no bd binary, and the Dolt database is gitignored and was never pushed, so the tracker was empty here: the ticket bodies existed on one machine only.

Install @beads/bd from npm (it ships win32 x64), initialise against the existing .beads/ without disturbing metadata.json's project_id, and make ticket state travel with the repo as .beads/issues.jsonl so any machine can read it after a git pull.

Deliberately NOT done: no Dolt push to the git remote, and no attempt to replace or reach the Mac's Dolt database. Cross-machine carry is JSONL interchange (upsert on import), which is additive and cannot clobber a database it never touches.
acceptance_criteria: bd --version works on Windows with no WSL; bd list runs against the repo's .beads/; .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in git and contains the open tickets; .beads/metadata.json project_id unchanged from the Mac's value; no-push is true so bd never pushes to origin unprompted.
notes: Observed 2026-09-18: npm i -g @beads/bd installed 1.3.0; bd init -p afox --skip-agents --skip-hooks --non-interactive reported 'Remote has no Dolt data yet; initialized a fresh local database'; metadata.json content identical to the pre-init copy apart from line endings; config.yaml untouched by init. --skip-agents was passed on purpose so bd could not rewrite the hand-written AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Observed on this Windows 11 machine 2026-09-18, no WSL. npm i -g @beads/bd installed 1.3.0; 'bd --version' prints 1.3.0 (f45b249ce) and 'bd where' resolves C:\_____\_CODE\afox\.beads. 'bd list' before init printed 'no beads database found' and wrote nothing, confirming the tracker was empty here and that nothing was overwritten. 'bd init -p afox --skip-agents --skip-hooks --non-interactive --role maintainer' reported 'Remote has no Dolt data yet; initialized a fresh local database'; --skip-agents kept it away from the hand-written AGENTS.md. .beads/metadata.json is byte-identical to the pre-init copy apart from line endings, so project_id f3529f2e-df73-4eae-a734-119313717e43 is unchanged; config.yaml was untouched by init. export.auto and export.git-add set true, no-push set true. 'bd export' wrote 8 issues to .beads/issues.jsonl and 'git check-ignore' confirms it is trackable. The Mac's Dolt database was never contacted: the only cross-machine channel configured is JSONL, which imports as an upsert.

title: Reconcile the Mac's Beads database into the repo
description:
The pre-existing tickets - afox-99q (the merge/review gate cycle), afox-2fc (pane lifecycle) and afox-5lf (v1 multiplexer) - live only in the Mac's Dolt database. It is gitignored, was never pushed, and the remote has no Dolt data, so their descriptions and acceptance criteria cannot be read from this machine.

They were deliberately NOT recreated here. Recreating them under their own ids would upsert over the Mac's originals on the next import and destroy acceptance criteria nobody can currently read; recreating them under new ids would leave permanent duplicates.

When the Mac is available: git pull there first so the Windows tickets arrive, bd import .beads/issues.jsonl (upsert, additive - it does not replace the database), then bd export so the JSONL carries the full set, and commit. After that both machines see everything and afox-2fc and afox-99q can be worked from either.

afox-5lf has no description and no acceptance criteria and reads as the original v1 umbrella epic. Decide then: close it as superseded, or rewrite it as the tracking epic for the Windows port.
acceptance_criteria: bd list on Windows shows afox-99q, afox-2fc and afox-5lf with the descriptions they were created with on the Mac; .beads/issues.jsonl in git contains every ticket from both machines; the Mac's Dolt database was added to, never replaced.

title: Run afox on Windows without WSL
description:
afox is zsh + tmux. Windows has neither, WSL is not installed and is not wanted. Three routes were considered; the ticket starts as a spike, not a build.

(a) MSYS2. pacman -S tmux zsh, fleet.sh runs close to unchanged. Cheapest by an order of magnitude. The whole route hangs on one unknown: whether a full-screen agent TUI (claude) renders correctly inside an MSYS2 tmux pane, or whether the ConPTY-to-MSYS-pty boundary mangles it. Spike this first on one pane before planning anything else.

(b) PowerShell + Windows Terminal. Rejected. wt.exe splits panes but offers no pane addressing, no capture-pane, no pane-border-format and no per-pane user options. Every mechanism afox depends on - roles on borders, send-keys, capture, cost display - has no equivalent.

(c) Own the PTY. A node host using node-pty/ConPTY spawns each provider and afox renders the panes itself. Gives real addressing, capture better than capture-pane, our own borders, and drops tmux and zsh entirely. The cost is honest and large: compositing several full-screen TUI agents means embedding a terminal emulator (xterm headless plus a renderer). That is writing a tmux. Only reach for it if (a) fails.

Decide (a) or (c) on the spike result, not on preference.
acceptance_criteria: Spike first: MSYS2 tmux installed, one pane running claude, and a capture-pane of that pane recorded showing whether the TUI is intact or corrupted. Then either a fleet spawned on Windows with every pane showing its role on the border, or a written finding that route (a) is dead and why, with the evidence.
notes:
SPIKE RESULT 2026-09-18: route (a) MSYS2 works. Route (c), writing our own terminal emulator, is not needed and should not be built.

Setup used, all without admin: msys2-x86_64-latest.tar.xz extracted to C:\Users\unmii\msys64, bootstrapped by running its bash from a native Windows process, then pacman -Sy --noconfirm --needed tmux zsh -> tmux 3.7c, zsh 5.9.2.

Observed, each from a live tmux server:
1. Rendering. claude.exe is a native Windows PE32+ console binary - the exact case the MSYS-pty boundary was expected to break. It renders correctly in an MSYS2 tmux pane: box-drawing rules, the trust menu, the selection marker, all intact in capture-pane output. No winpty shim needed.
2. Input. tmux send-keys Down moved the selection marker from 'No, exit' to 'Yes, I trust this folder'. The fallback channel afox relies on for non-claude panes works across the boundary.
3. Config resolution. Launched with -c /c/_____/_CODE/afox the pane came up already trusted and printed the banner with C:\_____\_CODE\afox, so claude.exe read credentials and trust from the Windows home despite MSYS $HOME being /home/yoga. Node's homedir() wins over the MSYS HOME, which is the behaviour afox wants.
4. Whole pipeline. FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 composed all five pane commands, the two user-style panes correctly wrapped in hold.sh, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR resolved to C:\Users\unmii\.claude.
5. Pane labelling. Three panes split, tiled, each given pane-scoped @role and @model, pane-border-status top and pane-border-format read back exactly as set.

Two prerequisites the spike turned up, both in afox-uvj: MSYS2 does not inherit the Windows PATH, so node is invisible until it is added; and ln -s produces a COPY by default even with Developer Mode on - MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict is required for a real symlink, which fleet.sh's ~/.tmux.conf handling depends on.

Not done and still open: no real fleet was spawned. Five billable sessions needs the user's word, and the spike's question was answered without it.

title: Replace uuidgen with node crypto.randomUUID in fleet.sh
description:
fleet.sh calls uuidgen to mint the --session-id it hands to claude and records in the cost manifest. uuidgen does not exist in Git Bash, MSYS2 or any stock Windows shell, so the call fails on Windows and takes the whole fleet window with it (a dying pane command makes tmux drop the window silently - the standing gotcha in README).

node is already a hard requirement of fleet.sh, so use it: node -e 'console.log(crypto.randomUUID())'. Same lowercase hyphenated form, one less binary to install.
acceptance_criteria: fleet.sh mints session ids without uuidgen on PATH; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh prints a well-formed lowercase UUID in each claude pane's --session-id.
notes: Change made 2026-09-18: fleet.sh now mints the session id with node -e 'process.stdout.write(crypto.randomUUID())'. Partially observed only - the node call itself was run on this Windows machine and printed 35511a4f-1d6a-46d5-a0b1-689f6dc0407c, but the acceptance criterion needs FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh, and fleet.sh is zsh, which is not installed here. Left in_progress rather than closed on an argument; it closes when a shell exists to run it in (afox-r0s).
close_reason: Observed 2026-09-18 on Windows 11, no WSL, in MSYS2 tmux. FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh printed --session-id 211981e0-b2d0-44cf-9530-4cb00cd6b8c3, c89da39b-4197-43fc-906b-8b01b1d2f7e7 and 9ea23a5d-581c-4ec2-94ea-5b7cb23a72eb for the three claude panes - well-formed lowercase v4 UUIDs, one per pane, with no uuidgen anywhere on PATH. Ran twice, via ./fleet.sh and via zsh ./fleet.sh, with different ids each time. Caveat recorded rather than glossed: the run was against an LF copy of the nine scripts in a temp directory, because the repo working tree is CRLF and roles.mjs cannot parse it (afox-l3s). The uuidgen replacement is independent of that and is proven.

title: Local test profile: whole fleet on ollama + goose
description:
roles.local.yml runs all five roles on goose + ollama + qwen3:8b, so the mechanism can be exercised without paying for five hosted sessions. Selected with FLEET_ROLES=roles.local.yml, which fleet.sh now supports.

Sized for this laptop: RTX 5070 Laptop with 8 GB VRAM and 32 GB RAM. qwen3:8b is Q4_K_M at 5.2 GB, fits in VRAM with room for the KV cache, and reports tools and thinking capability - goose needs tool calling, so a model without it is not a candidate however good its code is. Nothing else local qualified: ollama had only this model, and the HF cache is translation and chat GGUFs (NLLB, Helsinki-NLP, madlad, EuroLLM, RoLlama, Bielik, Samantha), no coding model among them. qwen2.5-coder:7b is the obvious alternate if a code-specific model is wanted; qwen3-coder:30b-a3b would be better at code but is ~18 GB at q4 and would spill to RAM, which five parallel panes cannot afford.

It is a rig for the mechanism, not a benchmark: one ollama server holds one copy of the model and all five panes queue on it.
acceptance_criteria: FLEET_ROLES=roles.local.yml spawns five panes, each labelled with its role, each idle at a ready prompt with no first user turn, and no hosted provider contacted.
notes: Observed 2026-09-18 on Windows in MSYS2 tmux: five panes, all dead=0, all held=0, each showing 'goose is ready' with an input prompt. Two corrections the run forced: 'goose run --system X -s' exits as soon as it has processed its input, so the pane closed and tmux dropped it - 'goose session --system X' is the interactive form and is what providers.yml now uses. And goose gates first use behind a telemetry consent prompt in every pane, the goose entry in README's 'every provider gates first use differently' list; the answer persists in AppData/Roaming/Block/goose/config/config.yaml, so it is a one-time cost per machine. Set to false here.
close_reason: Observed 2026-09-18 on Windows 11 in MSYS2 tmux. FLEET_ROLES=roles.local.yml spawned five panes; tmux list-panes reported ORCHESTRATOR, ARCHITECT, DEVELOPER, TESTER and REVIEWER, each [goose.qwen3:8b], all dead=0 and all held=0 - idle without hold.sh, because goose's --system is a real persona channel. Each pane showed 'goose is ready' with an input prompt and had taken no first turn. No hosted provider was contacted and nothing was billed. Two caveats recorded rather than glossed: the run used an LF copy of the scripts because the repo tree is CRLF (afox-l3s), and every pane came up in the MSYS home instead of the repo because of the path-form bug (afox-r66), which does not affect what this ticket claims but does block using the profile for real work.

title: Repository structure: modules and domain boundaries
description:
Root is flat: six markdown files, five .sh/.mjs scripts, three .yml, no boundaries. Proposal, deliberately sequenced after the typing decision so nothing gets moved twice:

  bin/                 entry point
  src/config|fleet|cost|board|gate/
  config/              roles.yml providers.yml prices.yml (user-editable, stays obvious)
  docs/                SPECS.md COMPARISON.md ACTIVE-LISTENING.md
  README.md AGENTS.md  stay at root

Three traps to respect:
- tmux.conf is the symlink target of ~/.tmux.conf. Moving it dangles every existing link. fleet.sh re-points the link on each run so it is survivable, but it needs a comment recording why.
- AGENTS.md and README.md must not move: every provider looks for them at the root.
- ${0:A:h}, roles.yml's repo: . and the manifest path are all path-derived. Each move is a real edit, not a git mv.
acceptance_criteria: Every script runs from its new location; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh composes identical pane commands before and after the move, diffed; a fresh clone plus setup.sh still produces a working fleet command.

title: Types for afox config: zod schemas over JSON, no decorators
description:
Original question was whether to convert afox into a TypeScript-with-decorators project resembling Java 21. Answer: no to the Java facsimile, yes to types.

Decorators would mean @Role({provider, tools}) classes, which moves per-role config out of roles.yml and back into code. That is a regression against SPECS #5 (per-role config), one of afox's strongest columns in COMPARISON.md, and against the role skill's own rule that roles are data. DI and annotations solve a problem five roles and no injection graph do not have.

What is worth doing: roles.mjs and cost.mjs each carry a separate hand-rolled mini-YAML parser, and fleet.sh uses a 0x1f-delimited field protocol (README gotcha 6) purely because that data crosses a shell boundary. One typed loader with zod schemas over JSON deletes both parsers and the delimiter trick, and gives a real error when a config field is wrong instead of silent garbage.

Open question the ticket must settle: JSON as the on-disk format costs roles.yml its comments and its prompt: | block scalars, which are the most readable part of the file today. Either keep YAML on disk and validate with zod after parsing, or move to JSON and accept losing the comments.
acceptance_criteria: A single typed config loader replaces the parsers in roles.mjs and cost.mjs; a malformed roles entry produces a named field error instead of a shifted field or an empty string; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 composes identical pane commands before and after the change, diffed.

title: roles.mjs swallows comments into block scalars
description:
A '#' comment line following a 'key: |' block was appended to the block's text. In roles.local.yml a two-line comment sitting between the peer block and roles: ended up inside every one of the five role prompts, shipped to the model.

Cause: block() continued the loop on isComment(line) at ANY indent, and then pushed the line because it is non-empty. A comment now ends the block like any other dedent.

Never bit roles.yml because it happens to have no comment directly after its peer block - which is luck, not design.
acceptance_criteria: A comment between a block scalar and the next key does not appear in the composed prompt, and the shipped roles.yml composes byte-identical pane commands before and after the change.
notes: Found by accident 2026-09-18 while dry-running the new local profile: the composed ORCHESTRATOR command contained '\#\ Prompts\ are\ shorter\ than\ roles.yml's\ on\ purpose...'. After the fix that string appears 0 times. Regression check: dry runs of the shipped roles.yml from a pre-fix tree and a post-fix tree, with session ids and tree paths normalised, diff clean.
close_reason: Fixed and regression-checked 2026-09-18. The composed ORCHESTRATOR command went from containing '\#\ Prompts\ are\ shorter\ than\ roles.yml's\ on\ purpose...' to 0 occurrences of that text. Regression: FLEET_DRY_RUN of the shipped roles.yml from a pre-fix tree (git HEAD) and a post-fix tree, session ids and tree paths normalised, diffed clean - 10 lines each, no difference.

title: goose --system is a real system-prompt channel
description:
Recorded because AGENTS.md's rule is that a flag existing is not a channel working, and this one was tested the way devin's --agent-config was.

goose run --system and goose session --system both take system instructions and both reach the model. providers.yml's goose entry is therefore prompt_style: system, not user, which means goose panes wake up idle and need no hold.sh. That makes goose the second provider after claude with a real persona channel, and it is the only local one.

Follow-up worth its own look: goose ships a bundled 'orchestrator' extension, disabled by default, described as 'Manage agent sessions: list, view, start, send messages, interrupt, and stop agents'. If that works between goose panes it would be peer messaging for non-claude roles, which SPECS 10 and 11 both record as the standing limit of the claude-only channel.
acceptance_criteria: Already met for the --system half. The orchestrator extension half is open: enable it on two goose panes and see whether one can message the other, or record that it cannot.
notes: Codename test 2026-09-18, goose 1.51.0 with ollama qwen3:8b: 'goose run --system "Your codename is TANAGER..." -t "What is your codename?"' answered TANAGER.

title: tmux pane borders are indistinguishable from pane content
description:
The lines separating panes render in the same colour and weight as the text inside them, so a five-pane fleet reads as one wall of text and it is hard to tell which agent said what.

Likely cause: borders draw in the default foreground on the same background as pane text, and pane-border-lines is at its default single. Candidate fix, all in tmux.conf: pane-border-lines heavy or double, pane-border-style fg dimmed, pane-active-border-style a bright fg plus bold, and reverse video on the role segment of pane-border-format so it reads as a title bar rather than a line of text.

Cheap and self-contained, but AGENTS.md is explicit that a styling claim is only real once seen on a live window - which on Windows means this waits for a working tmux.
acceptance_criteria: A live fleet window screenshot or capture showing pane borders clearly distinct from pane content, and the active pane distinct from the inactive ones. Every setting recorded in tmux.conf, never in ~/.tmux.conf.
